nodes.description: Reduced U2AF2 function changes exon usage in a subset of transcripts rather than abolishing splicing. In U2af50-deficient fly brain and in U2AF2-depleted human cell lines the affected set is enriched for transcripts encoding RNA-binding proteins, including Rbfox1 and other neurodevelopmental splicing regulators, and restoring Iswi, Rbfox1 or RpS19a partially rescues the fly brain phenotype. Which human neural transcripts carry the disease is not yet established.

nodes.description: Pan-neural, mushroom-body and motor-neuron knockdown of the fly U2AF2 ortholog, with rescue by wild-type or patient-variant human U2AF2.

A heterozygous de novo U2AF2 variant, usually a missense change in RNA recognition motif 1 or 2, alters the U2AF65 subunit that binds the polypyrimidine tract of 3' splice sites. The recurrent Arg149Trp, Arg150His and Arg150Cys substitutions lower the affinity of U2AF2 for a consensus polypyrimidine-tract RNA by roughly three- to five-fold by disrupting Arg146 contacts with the terminal nucleotide, without changing U2AF2 protein abundance or nuclear localization.
